title: Check for Prime
example:
n=17 → true
n=1 → false
n=9 → false
intuition: A prime has no divisor in 2..√n. Checking to n−1 wastes time (TLE on large n). For many queries, precompute a sieve.

approaches.title: Brute: trial to n-1
Optimal single-query: trial to √n
approaches.idea: Only need divisors ≤ √n; optionally skip evens after 2.

specialTechnique.title: Many queries? Sieve of Eratosthenes
specialTechnique.body: If you must answer primality for all values ≤ N, sieve in O(N log log N) time and O(N) memory — watch MLE if N is huge (e.g. 1e8 booleans).

complexity.time: O(√n) single query; sieve O(N log log N) preprocess

edgeCases: large primes near 1e12 for single check
patternRecognition: Constraints with Q queries up to N → sieve
followUps: Sieve memory layout (bitset) to reduce MLE?
interviewInsight: Connecting single-check √n vs sieve for many queries is the SDE-2 jump.
